tagline: A figure-eight on the Albemarle, with a horn for the ferry.
intro: The loop leaves Edenton on US 17 and crosses the Chowan River where it is nearly two miles wide. At low water, lines of old poles from the seine-fishing days stand off the shore. NC 45 and Sans Souci Road lead down to the Cashie, a river that runs its whole course in one county, where the byway crosses on a two-car cable ferry when it is running. From Windsor the road swings back by NC 308 and NC 32 over the Albemarle Sound to Edenton, 78 miles around.
William Byrd II came through Edenton in 1729 and counted perhaps 40 or 50 houses, adding that a citizen here was thought extravagant if he aspired to a brick chimney.

moments.title: Edenton
moments.text: On October 25, 1774, Penelope Barker and dozens of other women signed a resolve to drink no English tea, and a London newspaper answered with a satirical cartoon.

moments.title: Sans Souci Ferry
moments.text: The ferry is guided by a steel cable across the river, drivers on the far bank blow the horn to call it over, and the five-minute crossing saves a drive of about 20 miles.

moments.title: Windsor
moments.text: The Bertie County seat grew on Gray's Landing, a colonial trading point, and before the Civil War was a US port of entry on the road to Halifax.

practical: The Sans Souci ferry does not carry RVs or other large vehicles and does not run in high water or storms. The guidebook's alternate route backtracks to NC 308 and on to Windsor.
